instructions: Halve the 8 oz mushrooms, or slice them thickly if they're big. Mince the 2 garlic cloves and chop 2 tbsp of the parsley.

Cut each chicken breast in half horizontally, through the thickest part, so you have 4 thin cutlets. Lay them between two sheets of plastic wrap and pound them with a rolling pin or the bottom of a heavy pan until they're about 1/3 inch thick all over.
Season both sides with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper. Spread the 1/4 cup flour on a plate, press each cutlet into it and shake off the extra.

Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil and the 1 tbsp butter in a large heavy skillet over medium. When the butter foams, lay in the cutlets with room between them, in two batches if they don't fit. Leave them alone for 3 to 4 minutes, until they're golden underneath and let go of the pan.

Flip them and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes. You're cooking them to 160°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into one: it's done when it's white all the way through. Move them to a plate and cover loosely with foil.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil to the pan, then the mushrooms. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until their liquid has cooked off and they're golden brown.
Stir in the 1/2 tsp onion powder and the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Pour in the 3/4 cup Marsala and scrape up the brown bits from the bottom of the pan. Turn the heat up to medium high and boil it for 4 to 5 minutes, until most of it has cooked away.

Pour in the 3/4 cup broth, then stir in the 1/2 cup cream in a slow stream. Turn the heat down so it simmers and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until it's thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Stir in the remaining 1/4 tsp salt.
Slide the chicken back in with any juices from the plate and spoon the sauce over it. Simmer for about 2 minutes, until the chicken is hot through, then scatter the parsley over the top.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve with mashed potatoes, pasta or rice.
method_notes: All three pound thin chicken cutlets, dust them in seasoned flour and brown them in oil and butter, then brown mushrooms in the same pan and build a sauce of dry Marsala, chicken stock and cream before the chicken goes back in to warm through. Natasha's Kitchen reduces 3/4 cup Marsala almost completely before adding the stock and cream, and seasons with onion powder and garlic. Once Upon a Chef adds shallots and fresh thyme and simmers the wine, broth and cream together for 10 to 15 minutes, and RecipeTin Eats uses shallots and boils down a full cup of Marsala by half first. This one follows Natasha's Kitchen.
